literal: They do not know, everyone, thinking thus indeed, my love, in the street, wanders in distress, having become bewildered.
translation: Thinking 'no one knows of my secret', my love has become bewildered and wanders openly in distress in the public street.
modern: எல்லாரும் என் காதலைப் பற்றி அறியவில்லை என்று நினைத்து, என் காமமானது மருட்சியடைந்து தெருவிலே அலமந்து சுழல்கிறது.
explanation: The speaker describes how their intense love, which they tried to keep hidden, has now become public. Believing that no one else knew about this secret passion, the love itself has become bewildered and has spilled out into the public streets. The word 'maruku' has a double meaning: it refers to a public street and also means to be agitated or to whirl in distress. By saying 'marukiṉ marukum' (wanders in distress in the street), the poet brilliantly highlights how a deeply private grief has transformed into a highly visible public exposure.
